verdict.rationale: Mastra documents code-first workflows in TypeScript built from typed steps, retries, and branches. A community comment confirms these are written as chained method calls rather than YAML. Suspend/resume for human-in-the-loop implies persisted workflow state, but nothing explicitly documents automatic per-step checkpointing or durable recovery. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of automatic step checkpointing/durable resume after failure, and independent hands-on corroboration of checkpoint behavior.

support.subject: As a backend developer, I write workflows as ordinary code in my language — steps with automatic checkpointing — not YAML or a proprietary DSL

citations.quote: Compose typed steps, retries, and branches into production workflows your team can inspect and ship.
